overview.text: Today's artificial intelligence landscape features major corporate milestones, foundational research breakthroughs, and critical infrastructure updates. Anthropic made its official Nasdaq debut, while Claude Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in theoretical physics concerning black holes and quantum gravity. In research, new techniques explore looped language models that deepen reasoning at compact parameter counts by iterating a shared layer stack, alongside benchmarks like TabBioMed for structured biomedical tabular learning and shared n-gram embeddings in Chorus. Systems engineering also advanced significantly, highlighted by OpenAI's Performance Factory keeping ChatGPT fast using Codex-powered workflows, alongside the release of PostgreSQL 19 following an AI-reported vulnerability period. Finally, open-source model releases and developer toolkits continue to expand rapidly, ranging from unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF and HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM2-256M-Video-Instruct to Blender integrations, Google's Gemini 4 Neon pricing updates, and discussions surrounding hardware and local AI futures.

entries.title: Claude Fable 5.2 solves two open problems in the physics of black holes
entries.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 has solved two open problems in theoretical physics. Both concern black holes and the search for a theory of quantum gravity.

entries.title: Late Entry in Looped Language Models
entries.summary: Looped language models deepen reasoning at a compact parameter count by iterating a shared layer stack T times per token, turning recurrence depth directly into sequential decoding latency.
entries.why: Looped language models deepen reasoning at compact parameter counts by iterating a shared layer stack.

entries.title: Pete warden on local AI, open models, voice interfaces, the future of hardware
entries.why: Pete warden discusses local AI, open models, voice interfaces, and future hardware.

entries.title: TabBioMed: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Biomedical Tabular Learning
entries.summary: Recent advances in machine learning have accelerated biomedical prediction, but evaluation on structured biomedical data remains fragmented, especially for datasets with high dimensionality, large sample size, missingness, and class imbalance.
entries.why: TabBioMed provides a large-scale benchmark for structured biomedical tabular learning and missingness.

entries.title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
entries.summary: Autonomous LLM agents incur substantial cost and latency by invoking a large model (System-2) at every step, even when many intermediate actions choose among a small set of known candidates.
entries.why: This approach introduces a System-1 agent workflow to reduce the cost and latency of LLM calls.

entries.title: Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation
entries.summary: Language models can gain capacity at little computational cost from n-gram embedding tables: large tables of learned vectors for short sequences of consecutive tokens, which are looked up and added to the model's input or to its intermediate layers.
entries.why: Chorus adds capacity to language models at low computational cost using shared n-gram embedding tables.

entries.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
entries.summary: PostgreSQL 19 Released Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse.
entries.why: PostgreSQL 19 shipped with delays caused by addressing issues during the AI-reported vulnerability period.
